claim: The integrated stress response (ISR) is activated by phosphorylation of the translation initiation factor eIF2 in response to various stress conditions.
source: The integrated stress response (ISR) is activated by phosphorylation of the translation initiation factor eIF2 in response to various stress conditions.
evidence: This is a foundational statement about ISR activation mechanism, supported by established scientific knowledge and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Phosphorylated eIF2 (eIF2-P) inhibits eIF2's nucleotide exchange factor eIF2B.
source: Phosphorylated eIF2 (eIF2-P) inhibits eIF2's nucleotide exchange factor eIF2B, a twofold symmetric heterodecamer assembled from subcomplexes.
evidence: This is a well-established mechanism in ISR signaling, supported by prior knowledge and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: eIF2B is a twofold symmetric heterodecamer assembled from subcomplexes.
source: Phosphorylated eIF2 (eIF2-P) inhibits eIF2's nucleotide exchange factor eIF2B, a twofold symmetric heterodecamer assembled from subcomplexes.
evidence: This structural characterization is supported by prior structural studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: In the absence of eIF2B's α-subunit, the ISR is induced because unassembled eIF2B tetramer subcomplexes accumulate in cells.
source: In the absence of eIF2B's α-subunit, the ISR is induced because unassembled eIF2B tetramer subcomplexes accumulate in cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing ISR activation upon eIF2Bα depletion using the dTag13 system.

claim: Upon addition of ISRIB, eIF2B tetramers assemble into active octamers.
source: Upon addition of the small-molecule ISR inhibitor ISRIB, eIF2B tetramers assemble into active octamers.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro FRET data and analytical ultracentrifugation showing ISRIB-induced octamer formation.

claim: ISRIB inhibits the ISR even in the context of fully assembled eIF2B decamers.
source: Surprisingly, ISRIB inhibits the ISR even in the context of fully assembled eIF2B decamers, revealing allosteric communication between the physically distant eIF2, eIF2-P, and ISRIB binding sites.
evidence: This is supported by cellular experiments showing ISRIB effects in cells with intact eIF2Bα and fully assembled decamers.

claim: There is allosteric communication between the physically distant eIF2, eIF2-P, and ISRIB binding sites in eIF2B.
source: Surprisingly, ISRIB inhibits the ISR even in the context of fully assembled eIF2B decamers, revealing allosteric communication between the physically distant eIF2, eIF2-P, and ISRIB binding sites.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data showing mutual antagonism between eIF2-P and ISRIB binding, and structural analysis.

claim: A rocking motion in eIF2B couples the eIF2, eIF2-P, and ISRIB binding sites.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy structures suggest a rocking motion in eIF2B that couples these binding sites.
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM structural comparisons showing conformational changes between different ligand-bound states.

claim: eIF2-P binding converts eIF2B decamers into 'conjoined tetramers' with diminished substrate binding and enzymatic activity.
source: eIF2-P binding converts eIF2B decamers into 'conjoined tetramers' with diminished substrate binding and enzymatic activity.
evidence: This is supported by kinetic data showing reduced Vmax and increased KM upon eIF2α-P binding, and structural analysis.

claim: Canonical eIF2-P-driven ISR activation arises due to a change in eIF2B's conformational state.
source: Canonical eIF2-P-driven ISR activation thus arises due to this change in eIF2B's conformational state.
evidence: This is the central conclusion of the manuscript, supported by structural and biochemical data showing conformational changes.

claim: ISR activation has been linked to numerous human diseases, including cancer and neurological diseases.
source: ISR activation has been linked to numerous human diseases, including cancer and neurological diseases (reviewed in Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a review citation.

claim: Acute ISR activation largely plays a cytoprotective role.
source: While acute ISR activation largely plays a cytoprotective role, its dysregulation (both aberrant activation and insufficient activation) can negatively affect disease progression.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Many conditions of cognitive dysfunction have been linked causally to ISR activation in mouse models.
source: Many conditions of cognitive dysfunction, for example, have been linked causally to ISR activation in mouse models, including brain trauma resulting from physical brain injuries (Chou et al., 2017; Sen et al., 2017), familial conditions including Vanishing White Matter Disease and Down syndrome (Leegwater et al., 2001; van der Knaap et al., 2002; Zhu et al., 2019), neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) (Atkin et al., 2008; Ma et al., 2013), and even the cognitive decline associated with normal aging (Sharma et al., 2018; Krukowski et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies in mouse models.

claim: The ternary complex (TC) is composed of methionyl initiator tRNA (Met-tRNAi), eIF2, and GTP.
source: The TC is composed of methionyl initiator tRNA (Met-tRNAi), the general translation initiation factor eIF2, and GTP (Algire et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge about TC composition, supported by citation.

claim: At normal, saturating TC concentrations, translation initiates efficiently on most mRNAs containing AUG translation start sites.
source: At normal, saturating TC concentrations, translation initiates efficiently on most mRNAs containing AUG translation start sites; however, translation of some mRNAs is inhibited under these conditions by the presence of inhibitory small upstream open reading frames (uORF) in their 5′ untranslated regions (UTRs; Hinnebusch et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established mechanisms of translation regulation.

claim: When TC levels are sub-saturating, translation is repressed on most mRNAs.
source: When TC levels are sub-saturating, translation is repressed on most mRNAs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about translation regulation under stress.

claim: Some mRNAs containing uORFs in their 5′ UTRs are preferentially translated when TC levels are sub-saturating, including mRNAs encoding stress-responsive transcription factors such as ATF4.
source: In contrast, some mRNAs that contain uORFs in their 5′ UTRs are now preferentially translated, including mRNAs encoding stress-responsive transcription factors, such as ATF4 (Harding et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the discovery of ATF4 translational regulation.

claim: TC availability is a prime factor in determining the translational and transcriptional programs of the cell.
source: Thus, TC availability emerges as a prime factor in determining the translational and, consequentially, transcriptional programs of the cell.
evidence: This is an inference based on the described mechanisms of TC-dependent translation regulation.

claim: Loading of eIF2's γ subunit with GTP is catalyzed by the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) eIF2B.
source: Loading is catalyzed by the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) eIF2B, a large decameric and twofold symmetric enzyme that is composed of two copies each of five different subunits, eIF2Bα, β, δ, γ, and ε (Kashiwagi et al., 2016; Tsai et al., 2018; Wortham et al., 2014; Zyryanova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural and biochemical studies.

claim: eIF2B is composed of two copies each of five different subunits: eIF2Bα, β, δ, γ, and ε.
source: Loading is catalyzed by the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) eIF2B, a large decameric and twofold symmetric enzyme that is composed of two copies each of five different subunits, eIF2Bα, β, δ, γ, and ε (Kashiwagi et al., 2016; Tsai et al., 2018; Wortham et al., 2014; Zyryanova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Four upstream kinases (PKR, PERK, GCN2, and HRI) are activated by different stress conditions and phosphorylate eIF2 as a common target.
source: Stress sensing is accomplished by four upstream kinases (PKR, PERK, GCN2, and HRI) that are activated by different stress conditions and, in turn, phosphorylate eIF2 as a common target (Hinnebusch, 2005; Guo et al., 2020; Dey et al., 2005; Shi et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies characterizing these kinases.

claim: Phosphorylation by ISR kinases converges on a single amino acid, S51, in eIF2's α subunit (eIF2α).
source: Phosphorylation by each of these kinases converges on a single amino acid, S51, in eIF2's α subunit (eIF2α).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the phosphorylation site.

claim: eIF2α S51 phosphorylation converts eIF2 from eIF2B's substrate for GTP exchange into a potent eIF2B inhibitor.
source: As a profound consequence of eIF2α S51 phosphorylation, eIF2 converts from eIF2B's substrate for GTP exchange into a potent eIF2B inhibitor.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of ISR activation.

claim: eIF2 contacts eIF2B at four discontinuous interfaces (IF1–IF4).
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) studies of eIF2B•eIF2 complexes show that eIF2 snakes across the surface of eIF2B in an elongated conformation, contacting eIF2B at four discontinuous interfaces, which we here refer to as IF1–IF4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Kenner et al., 2019; Gordiyenko et al., 2019; Kashiwagi et al., 2019; Adomavicius et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to cryo-EM studies and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: IF1 and IF2 engage eIF2γ with eIF2Bε, sandwiching eIF2γ between eIF2Bε's catalytic and core-domain.
source: IF1 and IF2 engage eIF2γ (containing eIF2's GTPase domain) with eIF2Bε, sandwiching eIF2γ between eIF2Bε's catalytic and core-domain, respectively.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis from cited cryo-EM studies.

claim: The eIF2γ-eIF2Bε interaction pries the GTP binding site open, stabilizing the apostate to catalyze nucleotide exchange.
source: This interaction pries the GTP binding site open, thus stabilizing the apostate to catalyze nucleotide exchange.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural data about the mechanism of nucleotide exchange.

claim: IF3 and IF4 engage eIF2α across eIF2B's twofold symmetry interface.
source: IF3 and IF4 engage eIF2 via its α subunit across eIF2B's twofold symmetry interface, where two eIF2Bβδγε tetramer subcomplexes are joined.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis from cited cryo-EM studies.

claim: Upon S51 phosphorylation, eIF2α adopts a new conformation that renders it incompatible with IF3/IF4 binding.
source: Upon S51 phosphorylation, eIF2α adopts a new conformation that renders it incompatible with IF3/IF4 binding (Bogorad et al., 2017; Kenner et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2019; Kashiwagi et al., 2019; Adomavicius et al., 2019; Gordiyenko et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to structural studies.

claim: Phosphorylation unlocks an entirely new binding mode where eIF2α-P binds to a site between eIF2Bα and eIF2Bδ.
source: Rather, phosphorylation unlocks an entirely new binding mode on the opposite side of eIF2B, where eIF2α-P now binds to a site between eIF2Bα and eIF2Bδ.
evidence: This is based on structural studies showing the eIF2α-P binding site.

claim: The eIF2B decamer is built from two eIF2Bβδγε tetramers and one eIF2Bα2 homodimer.
source: The eIF2B decamer is built from two eIF2Bβδγε tetramers and one eIF2Bα2 homodimer (Wortham et al., 2014; Tsai et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: eIF2B subcomplexes are stable entities that readily assemble into decamers when mixed in vitro.
source: These subcomplexes are stable entities that, when mixed in vitro, readily assemble into decamers.
evidence: This is based on prior biochemical characterization.

claim: The eIF2Bβδγε tetramer has a low, basal GEF activity as it can only engage with eIF2 through IF1–IF3.
source: The eIF2Bβδγε tetramer has a low, basal GEF activity as it can only engage with eIF2 through IF1–IF3 (Tsai et al., 2018; Craddock and Proud, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to biochemical studies.

claim: eIF2B decamer assembly results in a greater than twentyfold rate enhancement of nucleotide exchange.
source: As expected, eIF2B decamer assembly results in a greater than twentyfold rate enhancement of nucleotide exchange, presumably due to enhanced substrate binding caused by the completion of the eIF2α binding site through the addition of IF4 (Tsai et al., 2018; Craddock and Proud, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to biochemical studies.

claim: eIF2Bα2 acts as an assembly-promoting factor for eIF2B decamer formation.
source: Assembly of the eIF2B decamer is driven by eIF2Bα2, which acts as an assembly-promoting factor.
evidence: This is based on prior biochemical characterization.

claim: ISRIB corrects cognitive deficits caused by traumatic brain injury in mice with no overt toxicity.
source: In mice, ISRIB corrects with no overt toxicity the cognitive deficits caused by traumatic brain injury (Chou et al., 2017), Down syndrome (Zhu et al., 2019), normal aging (Krukowski et al., 2020), and other brain dysfunctions (Wong et al., 2018) with an extraordinary efficacy, indicating that the molecule reverses the detrimental effects of a persistent and maladaptive state of the ISR.
evidence: This is supported by citations to mouse studies.

claim: ISRIB kills metastatic prostate cancer cells.
source: ISRIB also kills metastatic prostate cancer cells (Nguyen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a cancer study.

claim: ISRIB binds in a binding groove that centrally bridges the symmetry interface between eIF2Bβδγε tetramers.
source: ISRIB's mechanistic target is eIF2B to which it binds in a binding groove that centrally bridges the symmetry interface between eIF2Bβδγε tetramers (Sekine et al., 2015; Tsai et al., 2018; Zyryanova et al., 2018; Sidrauski et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: ISRIB acts as a 'molecular staple', promoting assembly of two eIF2Bβδγε tetramers into an enzymatically active eIF2B(βδγε)2 octamer.
source: As such, it acts as a 'molecular staple', promoting assembly of two eIF2Bβδγε tetramers into an enzymatically active eIF2B(βδγε)2 octamer.
evidence: This is based on structural and biochemical characterization of ISRIB function.

claim: Treatment with dTag13 led to rapid and complete degradation of FKBP12F36V-tagged eIF2Bα.
source: Treating ISR reporter cells with the small molecule dTag13 led to a rapid and complete degradation of FKBP12F36V-tagged eIF2Bα (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: eIF2Bα degradation was selective, as eIF2Bδ remained intact.
source: As expected, eIF2Bα degradation was selective, as eIF2Bδ, which binds directly to eIF2Bα in the decamer, remained intact.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 1B.

claim: dTag13 treatment did not increase eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: dTag13 treatment also did not increase eIF2α phosphorylation, a hallmark of canonical ISR activation by ISR kinases (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 1B.

claim: dTag13-induced eIF2Bα degradation led to increased translation of the ATF4 reporter and decreased translation of the general translation reporter.
source: Nevertheless, dTag13-induced eIF2Bα degradation led to increased translation of the ATF4 reporter and decreased translation of the general translation reporter (Figure 1C. Figure 1—figure supplement 4A) in a concentration-dependent manner.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: dTag13 treatment of cells lacking FKBP12F36V degron-tagged eIF2Bα did not induce the ISR.
source: dTag13 treatment of cells lacking FKBP12F36V degron-tagged eIF2Bα did not induce the ISR (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: ISRIB entirely reversed the ISR translational reprogramming by eIF2Bα depletion with an EC50 of 1.4 nM.
source: As predicted from previous in vitro work, ISRIB entirely reversed the ISR translational reprogramming by eIF2Bα depletion (EC50 = 1.4 nM; Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 4B; Tsai et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: eIF2Bα can be quantitatively replaced by ISRIB, rendering the eIF2B decamer and ISRIB-stabilized octamer functional equivalents in K562 cells.
source: Thus, eIF2Bα can be quantitatively replaced by ISRIB, a small molecule that causes eIF2B(βδγε)2 octamer assembly, rendering the eIF2B decamer and ISRIB-stabilized octamer functional equivalents in these cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing ISRIB can fully rescue eIF2Bα depletion.

claim: ISRIB inhibited eIF2-P-based stress induced by thapsigargin treatment only at early timepoints (1–3 hr), whereas at later timepoints ISRIB showed greatly diminished effects.
source: By contrast, ISRIB inhibited eIF2-P-based stress induced by thapsigargin treatment only at early timepoints (1–3 hr), whereas at later timepoints, ISRIB showed greatly diminished effects in blocking ISR activation.
evidence: This is supported by timecourse data in Figure 1E.

claim: Fluorescent protein tags do not interfere with eIF2Bβδγε tetramer stability.
source: Analysis by analytical ultracentrifugation following absorbance at 280 nm demonstrated that the fluorescent protein tags do not interfere with tetramer stability (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analytical ultracentrifugation data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Addition of eIF2Bα2 readily assembled fluorescently tagged eIF2Bβδγε tetramers into complete eIF2B decamers.
source: Moreover, consistent with our previous work, addition of separately expressed eIF2Bα homodimers (eIF2Bα2) readily assembled fluorescently tagged eIF2Bβδγε tetramers (eIF2Bβδγε-F) into complete eIF2B decamers.
evidence: This is supported by analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: Addition of ISRIB caused fluorescently tagged eIF2Bβδγε tetramers to assemble into octamers.
source: Similarly, the addition of ISRIB caused the tagged tetramers to assemble into octamers.
evidence: This is supported by analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: Half-maximal assembly of eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers occurs at 250 nM of ISRIB.
source: The results validated our system: in both cases, the FRET signal reliably reported on eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramer assembly into the respective larger complexes with half-maximal assembly (EC50) at 250 nM of ISRIB and 20 nM of eIF2Bα2 (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 2B.

claim: Half-maximal assembly of eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers occurs at 20 nM of eIF2Bα2.
source: The results validated our system: in both cases, the FRET signal reliably reported on eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramer assembly into the respective larger complexes with half-maximal assembly (EC50) at 250 nM of ISRIB and 20 nM of eIF2Bα2 (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 2C.

claim: eIF2Bα2 drives assembly of eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers into decamers with a t1/2 of 7 min.
source: Kinetic analysis showed that eIF2Bα2 drives assembly of eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers into decamers with a t1/2 of 7 min and that ISRIB drives eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers into octamers with similar kinetics (t1/2 = 5 min) (Figure 2D, E; 0–55 min time window).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic FRET data in Figure 2E.

claim: ISRIB drives eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers into octamers with a t1/2 of 5 min.
source: Kinetic analysis showed that eIF2Bα2 drives assembly of eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers into decamers with a t1/2 of 7 min and that ISRIB drives eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers into octamers with similar kinetics (t1/2 = 5 min) (Figure 2D, E; 0–55 min time window).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic FRET data in Figure 2D.

claim: eIF2Bα2-stabilized decamers dissociate slowly with a t1/2 of 3 h.
source: By contrast, the dissociation kinetics of eIF2Bα2-stabilized decamers and ISRIB-stabilized octamers differed substantially. Spiking in an excess of unlabeled eIF2Bβδγε tetramers to trap dissociated eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers into dark complexes revealed slow eIF2Bα2-stabilized decamer dissociation kinetics (t1/2 = 3 h), whereas ISRIB-stabilized octamers dissociated much faster (t1/2 = 15 min) (Figure 2D, E; 55–150 min time window).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic FRET data in Figure 2E.

claim: ISRIB-stabilized octamers dissociate with a t1/2 of 15 min.
source: By contrast, the dissociation kinetics of eIF2Bα2-stabilized decamers and ISRIB-stabilized octamers differed substantially. Spiking in an excess of unlabeled eIF2Bβδγε tetramers to trap dissociated eIF2Bβδγε-F tetramers into dark complexes revealed slow eIF2Bα2-stabilized decamer dissociation kinetics (t1/2 = 3 h), whereas ISRIB-stabilized octamers dissociated much faster (t1/2 = 15 min) (Figure 2D, E; 55–150 min time window).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic FRET data in Figure 2D.

claim: Co-treatment of ISRIB and eIF2Bα2 at saturating eIF2Bα2 concentrations did not induce greater complex assembly.
source: Still in vitro, as expected, co-treatment of ISRIB and eIF2Bα2 did not induce greater complex assembly when eIF2Bα2 was at saturating concentrations (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 2F.

claim: ISRIB substantially enhanced complex stability of eIF2B decamers, slowing the dissociation rate such that no discernible dissociation was observed.
source: However, ISRIB substantially enhanced complex stability, slowing the dissociation rate of the ISRIB-stabilized decamer such that no discernible dissociation was observed.
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 2F.

claim: Treatment with ISRIB at saturating eIF2Bα2 concentrations did not lead to a further increase in eIF2B's nucleotide exchange activity.
source: Consistent with these observations, treatment with ISRIB at saturating eIF2Bα2 concentrations did not lead to a further increase in eIF2B's nucleotide exchange activity as monitored by BODIPY-FL-GDP nucleotide exchange (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by BODIPY-FL-GDP exchange data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Degradation of eIF2Bα led to eIF2B complex disassembly as monitored by FRET signal.
source: Importantly, degradation of eIF2Bα via dTag13 treatment led to eIF2B complex disassembly, as monitored by FRET signal (Figure 3B), validating that our FRET system robustly reports on the eIF2B complex assembly state in living cells.
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 3B.

claim: At the 3 hr timepoint, the EC50 for eIF2B disassembly was 5 nM.
source: At the 3 hr timepoint, the EC50 for eIF2B disassembly was 5 nM (Figure 3B), which mirrors the EC50 for ISR activation (15 nM, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 3B.

claim: eIF2B's assembly state is intimately linked to translational output.
source: These data indicate that eIF2B's assembly state is intimately linked to translational output.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between assembly state and ISR activation.

claim: ISRIB assembled tetramers into octamers when the eIF2Bα subunit was not present.
source: ISRIB assembled tetramers into octamers when the eIF2Bα subunit was not present.
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 3C.

claim: In the presence of eIF2Bα, the FRET signal remained unchanged upon increasing ISRIB concentrations, indicating that the assembly state of eIF2B in K562 cells is largely decameric unless eIF2Bα is compromised.
source: Notably, in the presence of eIF2Bα, the FRET signal remained unchanged upon increasing ISRIB concentrations, indicating that the assembly state of eIF2B in K562 cells is largely decameric unless eIF2Bα is compromised.
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 3C.

claim: No decrease in FRET signal was observed upon ER stress or ISRIB treatment, arguing that eIF2B exists as a fully assembled decamer in both stressed and unstressed cells.
source: We observed no decrease in FRET signal upon ER stress or ISRIB treatment, arguing that eIF2B exists as a fully assembled decamer in both stressed and unstressed cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in Figure 3D.

claim: ISRIB resolved both eIF2-P-based activation of the ISR induced by thapsigargin and assembly-based activation of the ISR induced by eIF2Bα depletion.
source: Nevertheless, ISRIB resolved both eIF2-P-based activation of the ISR induced by thapsigargin and assembly-based activation of the ISR induced by eIF2Bα depletion (Figure 3E, lanes 4 and 6), implying that while ISRIB does not alter eIF2B's assembly state in the thapsigargin-treated cells, it still impacts ISR signaling.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 3E.

claim: In total cell lysate, eIF2α-P levels increased upon stress to a similar extent with and without ISRIB treatment.
source: Consistent with canonical ISR activation, in total cell lysate eIF2α-P levels increased upon stress to a similar extent with and without ISRIB treatment.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 4A.

claim: ATF4 translation occurred in stressed cells only, and ISRIB treatment inhibited ATF4 translation.
source: At the same time, ATF4 translation occurred in stressed cells only, and ISRIB treatment inhibited ATF4 translation (Figure 4A, Cell Lysate).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 4A.

claim: The amount of eIF2α-P bound to eIF2B was dramatically reduced in the immunoprecipitations from ISRIB-treated cells.
source: Surprisingly, we found that the amount of eIF2α-P bound to eIF2B was dramatically reduced in the immunoprecipitations from ISRIB-treated cells (Figure 4A, eIF2B-Bound).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data in Figure 4A.

claim: ISRIB antagonizes eIF2-P binding to eIF2B.
source: Thus, ISRIB antagonizes eIF2-P binding to eIF2B.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immunoprecipitation data showing reduced eIF2-P binding with ISRIB.

claim: The binding sites for ISRIB and eIF2-P are ~50 Å apart.
source: Because the binding sites for ISRIB and eIF2-P are ~50 Å apart, this result suggests an allosteric rather than an orthosteric interplay between ISRIB and eIF2-P binding.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the binding sites.

claim: eIF2-P, but not eIF2, competes with FAM-ISRIB for eIF2B binding.
source: Indeed, our results show that eIF2-P, but not eIF2, competes with FAM-ISRIB binding (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 4C.

claim: eIF2α-P alone, but not eIF2α, suffices to compete with FAM-ISRIB binding to eIF2B.
source: In fact, eIF2α-P, that is, eIF2's phosphorylated α-subunit alone, but not eIF2α, its unphosphorylated form, suffices in this assay (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 4D.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α by PKR over time converts it into eIF2α-P, which antagonizes ISRIB binding.
source: We confirmed this model with assays that used the eIF2 kinase PKR to phosphorylate eIF2α, thereby over time converting this previously inert component into eIF2α-P, the ISRIB binding antagonist (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic fluorescence polarization data in Figure 4E.

claim: Dephosphorylation of eIF2α-P by λ phosphatase over time destroyed its ability to dislodge FAM-ISRIB.
source: Conversely, dephosphorylation of eIF2α-P by λ phosphatase over time destroyed its ability to dislodge FAM-ISRIB (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic fluorescence polarization data in Figure 4F.

claim: ISRIB binding and eIF2α-P or eIF2-P binding are mutually exclusive events.
source: Together, these data show that ISRIB binding and eIF2α-P or eIF2-P binding are mutually exclusive events.
evidence: This is an inference based on the competition data from fluorescence polarization assays.

claim: eIF2-P inhibited eIF2B GEF activity in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: As previously shown, in nucleotide exchange assays that monitor eIF2B's GEF activity towards eIF2, eIF2-P inhibited eIF2B GEF activity in a concentration-dependent manner (Figure 5A; Wong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by BODIPY-FL-GDP exchange data in Figure 5A and citation.

claim: ISRIB partially rescued eIF2B GEF activity inhibited by eIF2-P.
source: ISRIB partially rescued the activity (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by BODIPY-FL-GDP exchange data in Figure 5C.

claim: The phosphorylated α subunit alone (eIF2α-P) inhibited eIF2B GEF activity.
source: Remarkably, the phosphorylated α subunit alone (eIF2α-P) inhibited eIF2B GEF activity (Figure 5B), and ISRIB again partially rescued activity (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by BODIPY-FL-GDP exchange data in Figure 5B.

claim: ISRIB partially rescued eIF2B GEF activity inhibited by eIF2α-P.
source: Remarkably, the phosphorylated α subunit alone (eIF2α-P) inhibited eIF2B GEF activity (Figure 5B), and ISRIB again partially rescued activity (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by BODIPY-FL-GDP exchange data in Figure 5D.

claim: The phosphorylated α subunit of eIF2 alone suffices to modulate eIF2B activity, and the remaining eIF2 subunits are dispensable for this effect.
source: Therefore, these data support the notion that the phosphorylated α subunit of eIF2 alone suffices to modulate eIF2B activity, that is, that orthosteric competition cannot wholly explain eIF2-P's inhibitory properties and that the remaining eIF2 subunits are dispensable for this effect.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing eIF2α-P alone can inhibit eIF2B.

claim: With increasing concentrations of eIF2α-P, Vmax decreased while KM increased.
source: Notably, with increasing concentrations of eIF2α-P, Vmax decreased while KM increased, suggesting that both substrate affinity and eIF2B catalytic activity were affected by eIF2α-P binding.
evidence: This is supported by Michaelis-Menten analysis data in Figure 6A.

claim: At near-saturating eIF2α-P concentrations, the kcat/KM ratio of inhibited eIF2B decamers approached that of the eIF2Bβδγε tetramer.
source: Intriguingly, at near-saturating eIF2α-P concentrations, the kcat/KM ratio, a measure of specific enzyme activity, approached that of the eIF2Bβδγε tetramer, suggesting that eIF2α-P inhibits the decamer by converting it to a tetramer-like state, rendering eIF2α-P-inhibited eIF2B decamers and eIF2B tetramers functionally equivalent (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: eIF2 readily bound to eIF2B with and without ISRIB.
source: eIF2 readily bound to eIF2B with and without ISRIB (lanes 1 and 2) but eIF2α-P addition reduced the amount of eIF2 recovered (lane 3).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 6C.

claim: eIF2α-P addition reduced the amount of eIF2 bound to eIF2B.
source: eIF2 readily bound to eIF2B with and without ISRIB (lanes 1 and 2) but eIF2α-P addition reduced the amount of eIF2 recovered (lane 3).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 6C.

claim: ISRIB inhibited eIF2α-P binding and restored normal eIF2 binding to eIF2B.
source: As expected, ISRIB inhibited eIF2α-P binding and restored normal eIF2 binding (lane 4).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 6C.

claim: FAM-ISRIB binding was blocked by the addition of eIF2α-P.
source: Consistent with the data shown in Figure 4E, F, eIF2B addition to FAM-ISRIB increased polarization (Figure 6D, black and red data points, respectively), and FAM-ISRIB binding was blocked by the addition of eIF2α-P (blue data point on the y-axis).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 6D.

claim: A titration of eIF2 into the reaction allowed FAM-ISRIB polarization to recover, indicating that eIF2 binds and disrupts eIF2α-P's inhibitory binding.
source: A titration of eIF2 into this reaction allowed FAM-ISRIB polarization to recover, indicating that eIF2 binds and disrupts eIF2α-P's inhibitory binding, which restores FAM-ISRIB binding.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 6D.

claim: eIF2 and ISRIB binding are synergistic, that is, positively coupled.
source: This result reinforces the notion that eIF2 and ISRIB binding are synergistic, that is, positively coupled.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing eIF2 can restore ISRIB binding.

claim: Apo-eIF2B has an overall very similar structure as the ISRIB-bound decamer.
source: This structure revealed that apo-eIF2B has an overall very similar structure as the ISRIB-bound decamer published previously (PDB ID: 6CAJ; Tsai et al., 2018; Zyryanova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM structural comparison.

claim: ISRIB slightly draws the decamer's two halves together by comparison with the apostate but does not induce marked changes in eIF2B's overall conformation.
source: Closer inspection revealed that ISRIB slightly draws the decamer's two halves together by comparison with the apostate but does not induce marked changes in eIF2B's overall conformation (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In the apo versus the ISRIB-bound state, eIF2Bδ L179 shifts slightly into the ISRIB binding pocket, occupying a position where it would clash with ISRIB binding.
source: In the apo versus the ISRIB-bound state, eIF2Bδ L179 shifts slightly into the pocket, occupying a position where it would clash with ISRIB binding, and eIF2Bβ H188 (a key ISRIB interactor) adopts a different rotamer (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B; Tsai et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Overlay of the apo decamer with structures of eIF2B bound to one or two copies of eIF2 revealed unremarkable changes.
source: Overlay of the apo decamer with structures of eIF2B bound to one or two copies of its enzymatically engaged substrate eIF2 also revealed unremarkable changes (Kashiwagi et al., 2019; Kenner et al., 2019; Gordiyenko et al., 2019; Adomavicius et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison with cited structures.

claim: The apo, ISRIB-bound, and eIF2-bound structures represent the enzymatically active state of eIF2B (A-State).
source: We infer from these results that all of these structures represent, with the minor variations noted, the enzymatically active state of eIF2B, henceforth referred to as the 'A-State' ('A' for active).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparisons.

claim: Overlaying the eIF2B-eIF2α-P structure with the A-State structures revealed significant changes in the overall architecture of eIF2B (I-State).
source: By contrast, overlaying the eIF2B-eIF2α-P structure (PDB ID: 6O9Z) with the A-State structures revealed significant changes in the overall architecture of eIF2B (Figure 7A), henceforth referred to as the 'I-State' ('I' for inhibited) (Kenner et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In the I-State, the two symmetrically opposed eIF2B tetramers have undergone a rocking motion that changes the angle between them by 7.5°.
source: In the I-State, the two symmetrically opposed eIF2B tetramers have undergone a rocking motion that changes the angle between them by 7.5° (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In the I-State, the ISRIB pocket is lengthened by ~2 Å.
source: The ISRIB pocket, consequentially, is lengthened by ~2 Å (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: In the I-State, the substrate-binding cleft between eIF2Bβ and eIF2Bδ′ is widened by 2.6 Å.
source: Critically, the substrate-binding cleft between eIF2Bβ and eIF2Bδ′, where the N-terminal domain of the unphosphorylated eIF2α substrate binds, is widened by 2.6 Å, pulling IF4 away but leaving IF1–IF3 as available binding surfaces (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: In the A-State, the cleft between eIF2Bα and eIF2Bδ′ is widened by 5.5 Å.
source: Conversely, in the A-State the cleft between eIF2Bα and eIF2Bδ′ is widened by 5.5 Å (Figure 7D), disrupting the eIF2-P binding site and suggesting a possible mechanism for the antagonism between eIF2-P and eIF2/ISRIB.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The A- to I-State transition is the central mechanism underlying ISR activation.
source: The A- to I-State transition thus appears to be the central mechanism underlying ISR activation.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript, based on structural and biochemical data.

claim: eIF2B adopts at least two notably distinct conformational states, the A- and I-States.
source: Based on these structural comparisons, we conclude that eIF2B adopts at least two notably distinct conformational states, the A- and I-States.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on structural analysis.

claim: The A- and I-States are mutually exclusive.
source: These two states are mutually exclusive (Figure 8).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural and biochemical data showing antagonism between ligands.

claim: The A- and I-States define an on-off switch of eIF2B's GEF activity.
source: The A- and I-States, therefore, define an on-off switch of eIF2B's GEF activity and can be thought of as functional equivalents to the decamer and tetramer assembly states, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional and structural data.

claim: Dysregulation of the ISR is increasingly implicated in numerous diseases with devastating consequences.
source: As dysregulation of the ISR is increasingly implicated in numerous diseases with devastating consequences, understanding the mechanism of ISR signaling is of profound importance (Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review.

claim: The central ISR regulatory hub is the decameric guanine nucleotide exchange complex eIF2B, which activates eIF2 by loading it with GTP.
source: The central ISR regulatory hub is the decameric guanine nucleotide exchange complex eIF2B, which activates eIF2 by loading it with GTP.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ISR regulation.

claim: Allosteric rather than clash-based orthosteric competition contributes significantly to eIF2-P-mediated inhibition.
source: Expanding from this notion, in this work we show that allosteric rather than clash-based orthosteric competition contributes significantly to eIF2-P-mediated inhibition.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the manuscript, supported by biochemical and structural data.

claim: eIF2 and eIF2-P binding are negatively coupled, even when only the α subunit of eIF2-P is present.
source: We show that eIF2 and eIF2-P binding are negatively coupled, even when only the α subunit of eIF2-P is present.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data showing competition between eIF2 and eIF2α-P.

claim: eIF2α-P binding impairs substrate binding even though the two binding sites are ~50 Å apart.
source: Thus, eIF2α-P binding impairs substrate binding even though the two binding sites are ~50 Å apart.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data and structural analysis.

claim: The phosphorylated form of eIF2's α subunit alone inhibits GEF activity both through reduced substrate affinity and reduced eIF2B catalytic efficiency.
source: Further, the phosphorylated form of eIF2's α subunit alone inhibits GEF activity both through reduced substrate affinity and reduced eIF2B catalytic efficiency.
evidence: This is supported by Michaelis-Menten kinetic analysis.

claim: The eIF2γ subunit is mechanistically dispensable for eIF2-P's inhibitory role.
source: With these data, we demonstrate that the eIF2γ subunit, which would be required for eIF2 inhibition via the clash-based orthosteric model, is mechanistically dispensable for eIF2-P's inhibitory role, although the added binding energy it contributes is certainly of importance in a cellular context.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on data showing eIF2α-P alone can inhibit eIF2B.

claim: Cryo-EM reconstructions reveal a rocking motion of the two eIF2Bβδγε tetramers with eIF2Bα2 acting as the fulcrum of the movement.
source: Cryo-EM reconstructions support this model. They reveal a rocking motion of the two eIF2Bβδγε tetramers with eIF2Bα2 acting as the fulcrum of the movement, akin to a butterfly raising and lowering its wings.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis of cryo-EM data.

claim: In the active A-State, eIF2Bβ and eIF2Bδ′ subunits are sufficiently close to fully shape the eIF2α binding site.
source: In the active or 'wings-up' A-State, eIF2Bβ and eIF2Bδ′ subunits are sufficiently close to fully shape the eIF2α binding site, thus allowing nonphosphorylated substrate engagement.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis.

claim: The A-State contains a properly sized ISRIB binding pocket, rendering eIF2 and ISRIB binding synergistic.
source: The A-State also contains a properly sized ISRIB binding pocket, thus rendering eIF2 and ISRIB binding synergistic.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis.

claim: In the A-State, the eIF2α-P binding site is misshapen and lacking properly positioned side chains critical for eIF2α-P binding.
source: In contrast, the eIF2α-P binding site is misshapen and lacking properly positioned side chains critical for eIF2α-P binding.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis.

claim: In the inhibited I-State, the eIF2α-P binding site is shaped correctly, while both the eIF2α and ISRIB binding sites are disrupted.
source: In the inhibited wings-down I-State, the eIF2α-P binding site is shaped correctly, while both the eIF2α (specifically IF4) and ISRIB binding sites are disrupted.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis.

claim: Models describing ISRIB's molecular function were exclusively focused on ISRIB's activity to promote eIF2B complex assembly prior to this work.
source: Prior to this work, models describing the molecular function of the drug-like small molecule ISRIB were exclusively focused on ISRIB's activity to promote eIF2B complex assembly.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge before this study.

claim: ISRIB can only exert its assembly-promoting function when eIF2Bα2 is limiting.
source: However, because eIF2Bα2 likewise has assembly-promoting activity, ISRIB can only exert this function when eIF2Bα2 is limiting.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mechanism of ISRIB action.

claim: Experimental depletion of eIF2Bα turned on ISR signaling in the absence of eIF2 phosphorylation.
source: Experimental depletion of eIF2Bα turned on ISR signaling in the absence of eIF2 phosphorylation, and ISRIB functionally substitutes for eIF2Bα2.
evidence: This is supported by cellular data showing ISR activation upon eIF2Bα depletion without eIF2 phosphorylation.

claim: ISRIB functionally substitutes for eIF2Bα2.
source: Experimental depletion of eIF2Bα turned on ISR signaling in the absence of eIF2 phosphorylation, and ISRIB functionally substitutes for eIF2Bα2.
evidence: This is supported by data showing ISRIB can rescue eIF2Bα depletion.

claim: Beyond a role in eIF2B assembly, ISRIB antagonizes eIF2-P binding.
source: In the context of saturating eIF2Bα2, we were thus left with a paradox regarding ISRIB's mechanism of action, which we resolve by showing that beyond a role in eIF2B assembly ISRIB antagonizes eIF2-P binding.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the manuscript, supported by biochemical data.

claim: eIF2B is predominantly a decamer in K562 cells.
source: While our data clearly show that eIF2B is predominantly a decamer in K562 cells, this leaves open the possibility that the assembly state differs by cell type and/or is regulated physiologically.
evidence: This is supported by FRET data in K562 cells.

claim: An ISRIB-stabilized eIF2B(βδγε)2 octamer is inert to inhibition by eIF2-P.
source: It is also important to note that an ISRIB-stabilized eIF2B(βδγε)2 octamer is inert to inhibition by eIF2-P.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structure and mechanism, as the octamer lacks the eIF2α-P binding site.

claim: ISRIB can affect the ISR in two modalities: by promoting eIF2B assembly under conditions where eIF2Bα2 is limiting and by biasing the conformational equilibrium of fully assembled decameric eIF2B towards the A-State.
source: We show that by binding to the same binding site on eIF2B, ISRIB can affect the ISR in two modalities: (i) by promoting eIF2B assembly under conditions where eIF2Bα2 is limiting or decamer stability may be compromised and (ii) biasing allosterically the conformational equilibrium of fully assembled decameric eIF2B towards the A-State, rendering inhibition by eIF2-P more difficult.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the manuscript, supported by cellular and biochemical data.

claim: In vanishing white matter disease, point mutations destabilize the eIF2B complex and ISRIB may provide primarily a stabilizing effect to recover eIF2B function.
source: In the case of vanishing white matter disease, for example, point mutations destabilize the eIF2B complex and ISRIB, therefore may provide primarily a stabilizing effect to recover eIF2B function (Wong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is speculation based on the mechanism and supported by citation.

claim: In traumatic brain injury, sustained cognitive dysfunction is caused by persistent canonical ISR activation through eIF2-P.
source: By contrast, in traumatic brain injury, sustained cognitive dysfunction is caused by persistent canonical ISR activation through eIF2-P (Chou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a study on traumatic brain injury.

claim: In traumatic brain injury, ISRIB would primarily counteract the aberrant ISR activation by predisposing eIF2B to the A-State.
source: Hence, ISRIB would primarily counteract the aberrant ISR activation by predisposing eIF2B to the A-State.
evidence: This is speculation based on the mechanism of ISRIB action.

claim: The AcP10 protein in the Bw-CoV SW1 virus interacts with eIF2B to exert an ISRIB-like effect, likely predisposing eIF2B to the A-State.
source: The AcP10 protein in the Bw-CoV SW1 virus, for example, interacts with eIF2B to exert an ISRIB-like effect, likely predisposing eIF2B to the A-State (Rabouw et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a study on viral proteins.
